evals.name: sequential-cli
evals.prompt: i have a CLI that reads a csv, validates rows, calculates totals, writes a report and exits. someone suggested xstate for its lifecycle. sketch the smallest sensible design and explain whether to use it.
assertions: Keeps ordinary sequential functions rather than introducing named states or a statechart runtime
Separates parsing and calculations from file access
Names a concrete additional requirement before considering lifecycle machinery

evals.name: tycoon-entity-lifecycles
evals.prompt: design a tycoon game core: factories build, produce, break and repair; workers choose jobs based on distance/pay, travel, work and rest. inventory/cash change each tick. would one big state machine work? propose the smallest suitable structure.
assertions: Separates factory and worker lifecycles rather than enumerating global combinations
Keeps job scoring and economic calculations outside lifecycle states
Keeps cash, inventory and progress as data rather than enumerating their values as states
Justifies any statechart library with a concrete required runtime feature, or keeps plain transition functions

evals.name: approval-agent-recovery
evals.prompt: design an email agent that drafts, waits for human approval, edits on feedback and sends. approvals may arrive late; drafts may change; users cancel; provider results arrive later; process can restart. can a statechart handle it? what owns decisions, effects, recovery and tests?
assertions: Separates model proposals, authoritative lifecycle decisions and external effects
Approval binds to an exact draft revision and edits invalidate approval
Defines handling of stale approvals and late provider results after cancellation
Does not claim local cancellation reverses an external send already accepted
Defines persistence and effect recovery separately from legal transitions
Justifies any statechart runtime with a required feature, or keeps a typed transition function
Tests event sequences and recovery boundaries
